topics.concept: TAM is everyone who could ever buy, SAM is the slice you can actually reach, and SOM is the share you can realistically win. Each layer needs its own math: top-down from industry figures or bottom-up from customer counts times price. The discipline is documenting every assumption so the number can be challenged.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded market with customer counts, prices, and reach filters, computes TAM, SAM, and SOM by both top-down and bottom-up methods, and lists assumptions.
topics.name: TAM SAM SOM Estimator
topics.real_world_use: Founders size markets in pitch decks with TAM, SAM, and SOM layers.

topics.concept: Survey analysis starts with cleaning: removing speeders, straight-liners, and incomplete responses that pollute results. Then come the descriptives: distributions, top-two-box scores, and cross-tabs by segment. The analyzer automates the boring parts so the analyst spends time on what the patterns mean.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded survey responses with planted quality issues, cleans them, and computes distributions, top-two-box scores, and segment cross-tabs.
topics.name: Survey Response Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Market researchers clean and tabulate survey data before writing insight reports.

topics.concept: A competitor feature matrix lists capabilities as rows and competitors as columns, marking who has what. Gaps where nobody delivers are opportunities; rows where everyone matches are table stakes. The matrix turns scattered competitive intel into one comparable view.
topics.data_idea: Builds a seeded feature set across competitors with presence scores, renders the matrix, and highlights uncontested gaps and parity rows.
topics.name: Competitor Feature Matrix
topics.real_world_use: Product teams maintain feature matrices to position against rivals in sales cycles.

topics.concept: A buyer persona distills a segment into goals, pains, buying triggers, and decision criteria. Personas built from real interview quotes beat demographic stereotypes. The builder assembles cards from seeded notes and ties each persona to the messages that resonate.
topics.data_idea: Creates seeded interview notes per segment, synthesizes persona cards with triggers and criteria, and maps personas to value propositions.
topics.name: Buyer Persona Builder
topics.real_world_use: B2B marketers build personas to target campaigns and tailor messaging.

topics.concept: Pricing sensitivity testing asks buyers what they would pay, then looks at where too-cheap doubts and too-expensive rejections cross. The acceptable range sits between those curves. Even a simplified version beats guessing a price from cost-plus math.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded willingness-to-pay responses, plots too-cheap and too-expensive curves, and reports the acceptable price range and optimal point.
topics.name: Pricing Sensitivity Explorer
topics.real_world_use: Pricing teams run sensitivity studies before launching new tiers.

topics.concept: The van Westendorp method asks four price questions: too cheap, bargain, expensive, and too expensive. Plotting the cumulative curves reveals the optimal price point where expensive and bargain cross, plus the acceptable range. It is the classic pricing research technique for a reason: it is simple and directional.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded answers to the four van Westendorp questions, builds the cumulative curves, and computes the optimal price point and indifference range.
topics.name: Van Westendorp Price Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Consumer brands use van Westendorp studies to set launch prices.

topics.concept: Conjoint analysis presents buyers with product profiles that trade off features and price, then infers how much each attribute is worth from their choices. The output is part-worth utilities: the value of each feature level. It answers what customers will pay for, not just what they say they like.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded choice tasks across attribute profiles, estimates part-worth utilities from choices, and ranks attributes by importance with willingness-to-pay.
topics.name: Conjoint Analysis Lite
topics.real_world_use: Product teams use conjoint results to decide which features justify a price premium.

topics.concept: Market share tracking divides each competitor's revenue or units by the total market each period. Share shifts reveal who is winning before revenue totals do. The tracker plots share trends and flags statistically meaningful moves versus noise.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded market revenues per competitor over periods, computes share trends, and flags significant share shifts with confidence bands.
topics.name: Market Share Tracker
topics.real_world_use: Strategy teams track share quarterly to measure competitive momentum.

topics.concept: Sentiment tallying counts positive, negative, and neutral mentions across reviews and social posts, then tracks the mix over time. Theme extraction groups the negatives so product teams know what to fix. Volume spikes around launches show whether reception is warming or souring.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded mentions with sentiment labels and themes, tallies sentiment mix over time, and surfaces rising negative themes.
topics.name: Sentiment Tally Monitor
topics.real_world_use: Brand teams monitor sentiment around launches to catch PR problems early.

topics.concept: Win-loss interviews ask buyers why they chose a competitor or stayed out, and coding turns transcripts into countable themes. The coder tags each interview with reasons, then aggregates by segment and competitor. Patterns across interviews become strategy; single anecdotes stay anecdotes.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded interview transcripts with reason mentions, codes them against a reason taxonomy, and aggregates win and loss drivers by segment.
topics.name: Win-Loss Interview Coder
topics.real_world_use: Product marketing codes win-loss interviews to sharpen competitive positioning.

topics.concept: Churn surveys ask departing customers why they left and what would have kept them. Coding the answers separates fixable causes, like onboarding gaps, from structural ones, like budget cuts. The analyzer quantifies each cause and estimates the revenue recoverable by fixing the top ones.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded churn responses with coded reasons, aggregates cause frequencies, and estimates recoverable revenue per fixable cause.
topics.name: Churn Survey Analyzer
topics.real_world_use: Retention teams prioritize fixes from churn survey analysis by recoverable revenue.

topics.concept: MaxDiff asks respondents to pick the most and least important item from small sets, repeating across many sets. Counting best-minus-worst scores ranks a long feature list with far less effort than rating each one. It is the efficient way to prioritize when everything claims to be important.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded MaxDiff choice sets and picks, computes best-worst scores per item, and ranks features by relative importance.
topics.name: MaxDiff Priority Simulator
topics.real_world_use: Researchers use MaxDiff to rank dozens of features when surveys must stay short.

topics.concept: Price elasticity measures how much quantity falls when price rises: elastic demand drops fast, inelastic barely moves. Estimating it from historical price and volume data guides whether a price increase grows or shrinks revenue. The model fits the elasticity curve and simulates revenue at candidate prices.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded price and quantity history with noise, estimates elasticity by regression, and simulates revenue across a price grid.
topics.name: Price Elasticity Model
topics.real_world_use: Revenue managers set prices from elasticity estimates to maximize total revenue.

topics.concept: Market entry scoring rates candidate markets on size, growth, competition, fit, and risk, then weights the factors into one score. The weights encode strategy: a land-grab favors size, a niche play favors fit. Sensitivity on the weights shows whether the winner is robust or an artifact.
topics.data_idea: Builds seeded market profiles with factor scores, applies weighted scoring, ranks markets, and tests rank stability under weight changes.
topics.name: Market Entry Scorer
topics.real_world_use: Corporate strategy teams score markets to sequence geographic expansion.

topics.concept: A brand tracking index combines awareness, consideration, and preference into one composite measured each wave. Component trends show whether marketing builds the funnel or just rents attention. The tracker normalizes components, weights them, and reports the index with wave-over-wave change.
topics.data_idea: Simulates seeded brand survey waves with awareness and preference metrics, computes the composite index per wave, and decomposes changes by component.
topics.name: Brand Tracking Index
topics.real_world_use: CMOs report brand indices to boards as the long-term return on marketing.

topics.concept: Segmentation clusters customers by behavior and needs so marketing can treat different groups differently. The lite version runs k-means on seeded behavioral features, profiles each cluster, and names the segments in plain language. Good segments are measurable, reachable, and genuinely different.
topics.data_idea: Generates seeded customer features with planted segments, clusters them, profiles each cluster's behavior, and validates segment separation.
topics.name: Customer Segmentation Lite
topics.real_world_use: Marketing teams segment bases to personalize campaigns and offers.
